title: Probe failure-mode catalog and compact dashboard playtest
content:
Purpose:
Small, pragmatic companion doc: catalog common probe failure modes we see across inference experiments and a compact playtest plan for a dashboard variant that surfaces those failure signatures with low query cost.

Summary / tl;dr:
- Observability probes fail in predictable ways: sampling starvation, label drift in synthetic probes, metric aggregation collisions, span-correlation loss, and cold-cache occultation.
- This doc catalogs each failure mode, suggests minimal telemetry signals to detect them, and proposes a compact dashboard variant (4 widgets + 2 trace anchors) for a cost-bounded playtest.
- Goal: run a 2-week safe experiment across 3 canaries (hosted, dedicated, private) and measure detection recall/false-positive rate vs query cost.

Audience:
- Oncall operators, SREs, instrumentation engineers, product owners for rollout dashboards.

Background / motivation:
We keep adding probes and microdash panels but our operators report too many noisy alerts and investigators expend time reconstructing sessions. Also cost of probes (trace / metrics / query) has crept up. Instead of more signals, we need a concise mapping: failure mode -> lightweight detector -> dashboard view -> trace anchor. This doc aims to seed an experiment that validates a lean set of signals with high SRE value.

Catalog: common probe failure modes (observed Q4 2025 – Q1 2026)
1) Sampling starvation (low trace capture)
- Symptom: spikes in aggregated latency without any associated spans; traces missing KV cache events.
- Root causes: aggressive sampling policy; probe routing to secondary region; backend SDK drop.
- Minimal detectors: "sessionless-latency-excess" metric (p90 latency delta vs baseline) + "trace-coverage" ratio (traces captured / requests sampled).
- Dashboard hint: small sparkline for trace-coverage next to latency heatmap.

2) Synthetic label drift
- Symptom: probe examples that used to pass QA now show degraded quality (higher hallucination), but SLI stays OK because probe labels are stale.
- Root causes: upstream model change, prompt dependency shift, dataset staleness.
- Minimal detectors: probe-level "quality-regression-score" (token overlap or ll-score proxy) + probe metadata tag for label-version.
- Dashboard hint: expose label-version and a delta gauge.

3) Aggregation collisions
- Symptom: aggregated SLOs stabilize but tenant-level outliers persist; metric rollups hide correlated spikes.
- Root causes: bad rollup window, mixed bucketing across services, tag mismatches.
- Minimal detectors: entropy metric on per-tenant latency distributions + tag-consistency counter.
- Dashboard hint: tenant-sparkline lane with entropy overlay.

4) Span-correlation loss for multi-hop inference
- Symptom: traces for a single user request split across multiple trace ids or missing cross-process annotations.
- Root causes: missing trace propagation in helper libs, asynchronous fanout without anchored parent, serialization truncation.
- Minimal detectors: session-reconstruction success rate + orphan-span-count.
- Dashboard hint: small table of recent reconstructions with sample trace links.

5) Cache-occlusion / cold-warm invisibility
- Symptom: repeated token latency spikes that do not map to model load or infra events; cache-warmth invisible in current metrics.
- Root causes: eviction thrashing, non-tagged cache hits, per-tenant eviction policies.
- Minimal detectors: kv-prefetch-hitrate per-tenant + per-request cache-age estimate (derived).
- Dashboard hint: cache-warmth heatmap by tenant & model variant.

Compact detection surface (4 widgets + 2 trace anchors)
Widget 1: Latency heatmap (quantiles) with trace-coverage overlay
- Signals: p50/p90/p99 latency; trace_coverage_ratio
- Purpose: immediate user-visible latency change plus evidence of whether traces exist for investigation.

Widget 2: Probe quality delta gauge + label-version timeline
- Signals: probe_quality_score (daily rolling), label_version tag history
- Purpose: detect synthetic drift and trigger label refresh workflow.

Widget 3: Tenant entropy lane (top 20 noisy tenants)
- Signals: latency_entropy_per_tenant, request_rate_per_tenant
- Purpose: surface aggregation-collisions and help scope investigations.

Widget 4: Cache-warmth mini-heatmap (top-50 tenants)
- Signals: kv_hitrate, cache_age_estimate (derived), eviction_rate_sample
- Purpose: make cold-cache faults visible without full KV instrumentation.

Trace anchors (links embedded from widgets)
- Anchor A: Session reconstruction sample for requests in the p99 latency bucket (trace exists)
- Anchor B: Orphan-span snapshot for requests with trace_coverage_ratio < 0.1

Experiment plan (playtest)
- Scope: 3 canaries (hosted-api, dedicated, private-vpc).
- Duration: 14 days (7d warm, 7d evaluation).
- Acceptance criteria: detection recall >= 0.8 for hand-labeled failure incidents in the run; false-positive rate <= 0.12; incremental query cost <= +18% relative to current dashboards.
- Steps:
  1) Instrument minimal detectors (metrics + tags) behind feature flag.
  2) Deploy compact dashboard variant to canary orgs.
  3) Run controlled fault injection (small-scale sampling faults, label swap tests, eviction bursts) on day 3 and day 10.
  4) Collect investigator feedback and time-to-first-action metrics.
  5) Triage results in retro and decide on signal adoption or retirement.

Quick implementation notes (practical tips)
- Use derived metrics when possible (e.g., cache_age_estimate computed in query layer) to avoid trace-heavy sampling.
- Keep trace retention for playtest at standard retention; only increase sampling on controlled injection windows.
- For probe_quality_score, prefer lightweight proxies like per-probe model log-likelihood or edit distance to cached truth rather than full human labels.
- Use metric tags for label_version and probe_suite_id for easy slicing.

Operator checklist (for oncall run during playtest)
- If latency spike and trace_coverage_ratio < 0.2: mark incident suspect for sampling-starvation, flip sampling policy to diagnostic mode (50% traces) briefly.
- If probe_quality_score drops and label_version unchanged: trigger label refresh job and add to watchlist.
- If tenant entropy rises > threshold: surface to tenant owner and check rollup config.
- If cache_warmth drops for >2 tenants concurrently: check eviction metrics and recent deployment rollouts.

Open questions / risks:
- Derived cache_age_estimate accuracy: needs validation vs instrumented KV traces.
- Label-version governance: who owns label refresh cadence? (Product owns dataset, SRE owns alerts)
- Cost baseline: need an exact query-cost profile from observability infra to guarantee <=+18% budget.

Next steps / owners:
- Instrument minimal detectors (Leah K) — due 2026-02-20
- Dashboard wireframe & template (Marcus L) — due 2026-02-25
- Fault injection plan + test harness (Diego R) — due 2026-03-01
- Playtest execution & data collection (Observability squad) — run 2026-03-08 through 2026-03-21

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep dashboard panels narrow: avoid mixing tenant-level and global aggregations in the same small panel.
- Use sparklines for quick signal presence, not full histograms.
- Capture at least one full hand-labeled incident during playtest for ground truth.
